Ford Ranger in Danger? Vietnamese Firm Rolls Out the $33,000 Wild Pickup Truck
7 photos
Photo: VinFast
While the Chinese are struggling to make their way into the United States, Vietnam has the doors wide open and rolls out yet another model. This time, it is giving the Ford Ranger a run for its money, transforming the segment into a battleground of styles and powertrains with its latest VF Wild. A planned factory in North Carolina, currently slated for 2028 at the earliest, was supposed to help them position their models more competitively.
While America is trying to keep Chinese cars at bay, the Vietnamese seem to be going all in. VinFast’s Wild is ready to take on the Ford Maverick, Ranger, and upcoming Fathom, as well as Slate’s pickup truck. The United States has locked the Chinese out of the country with massive tariffs and restrictions on connected vehicles, software, and hardware linked to China.
But VinFast comes all the way from Vietnam to steal the show from popular or expected-to-become-popular pickup trucks. The Wild has just hit its home market, Vietnam, with a starting price of 860 million VND, which translates to roughly $33,000, Autoblog reports . To keep up with the East, Ford is already working on another affordable pickup truck, set to be launched after the arrival of the Fathom.
That would place it right beside the Ford Ranger , which starts around $33,500. It would be more expensive than the Maverick (around $28,145) and the upcoming Fathom ($28,350), while the Slate truck is the most affordable of the pack at $24,950.
Photo: VinFast The concept that previewed the model was electric, but the VinFast VF Wild strays away from its all-electric roots. Instead, it features a 1.5-liter range extender and an electric motor that produces 215 horsepower (218 metric horsepower).
The 46.4 kWh LFP battery stores enough energy for a drive of up to 155 miles (250 kilometers) on electric power only before the truck needs to be plugged in again. The Wild can roll up to 620 miles (1,000 kilometers) with the tank and battery full.
The battery supports 6.6 kW AC charging and up to 90 kW DC fast charging, taking 30 to 32 minutes to charge from 10% to 70%. It also includes Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) technology to power external tools and camping appliances.
The model measures 211.6 inches (5,376 millimeters) in length, which means it is slightly longer than Ford’s Ranger (210.6 inches or 5,349 millimeters) and far larger than the Maverick (199.7 inches or 5,072 millimeters). The numbers make it slightly larger than both of Ford’s entry-level pickups.
Photo: VinFast The VF Wild comes with a payload of 1,653 pounds (750 kilograms), which is very similar to that of the Ford Ranger: 1,711 pounds (776 kilograms). The Vietnamese truck’s towing capacity has yet to be announced. Unlike the Ford Ranger, the Wild is 2WD only.
The Wild features a minimalist interior, with a 10-inch touchscreen that controls most of the vehicle’s onboard functions, and reclining second-row seats to maximize passenger space. Just like the Tesla Model 3 and VinFast VF 3, the VF Wild ditches the traditional driver instrument cluster and head-up display.
The gear selector sits on a stalk behind the flat-bottomed steering wheel, freeing up space on the center console for storage compartments and cupholders. Built-in tech includes a contextual voice assistant, over-the-air firmware updates, battery health monitoring, and remote vehicle controls via smartphone or smartwatch apps.
VinFast has not announced an official U.S. release date for the VF Wild, and it may not arrive in America until 2028 or later. VinFast only sells two electric SUVs in the United States: the VF 8 , which starts at $41,790 with the destination fees included, and the six- or seven-seat VF 9, which costs $64,290.
Photo: VinFast For the VF 8, the price includes a complimentary VinFast home charger and VinFast e-bike, alongside 0% APR financing offers for up to 84 months. The automaker has delayed the smaller VF 6 and VF 3, while the VF 3, already delayed multiple times, should arrive in the United States as a tiny, two-door micro-SUV, expected to kick off at under $20,000. For the moment, the model remains on indefinite hold for the U.S. market.
Every VinFast sold in America is currently imported from Hai Phong, Vietnam. Without a U.S. assembly plant, bringing a pickup like the VF Wild to America would trigger the 25% "Chicken Tax" applied to foreign-built light trucks (pickup trucks and cargo vans. This would make it nearly impossible for the firm to price it competitively.
To offset tariffs, VinFast is planning to build a plant in Moncure, North Carolina. Originally scheduled to open in July 2024 and later pushed to 2026, the plant was rescheduled to start operating in 2028 at the earliest, as the company cited slow U.S. EV demand.
Aside from clearing and grading the 1,765-acre site, VinFast has not erected any factory buildings. Furthermore, in May 2026, North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson sued VinFast for breaching its development contract. The state is exercising its contractual right to buy back the industrial megasite so it can offer the land to another company. VinFast is fighting the lawsuit in court.
